A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same language-supervised view-selection work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary sections are readable and matchable despite renaming and reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original experiments on Ego-Exo4D and LEMMA, human evaluations, ablations, and supplementary analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds captioner-count experiments, three-split evaluation, and visual and concept-frequency analyses.

M1.justification: The captioner-based pseudo-labeler, rank aggregation, view classifier, auxiliary pose predictor, and training losses remain unchanged. LANGVIEW names the existing framework; the new two-captioner experiment is an ablation, not a replacement of the proposed three-captioner method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Ego-Exo4D and LEMMA with the same activity and camera coverage. The single-exo-camera experiment already appears in v2, Section 6.6/Table 7, and becomes Section 7.2/Table 8 in v3. New splits and analyses remain within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same baselines, including Hand-object, Body-area, Snap angles/Pixel-objectness, and Longest-caption. New analyses reuse Body-area. The newly cited Switch-a-view is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: v3 adds evaluation over three disjoint Ego-Exo4D test splits in Section 8/Table 9 and a two-captioner experimental condition in Table 7. Existing preprocessing, metrics, primary model settings, and human-study sample counts remain unchanged. The new split construction is not detailed.

E4.justification: v3 adds attention heatmaps for two clips, a two-captioner condition extending the existing aggregation ablation, and performance analysis against training verb-noun frequency (Figures 5 and 8; Table 7). These targeted diagnostics supplement the retained ablations, feature visualizations, ranking analyses, and failure examples.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 newly reports 78.5% inter-evaluator agreement, and Table 9 introduces averaging across three disjoint test splits. Existing significance statements remain. No seed information, dispersion estimates, or confidence intervals are added; the PDFs do not establish increased repeated training runs.

E6.justification: Previously reported table values are retained. New Table 7 reports two-captioner results, including 13.3 CIDEr and 34.2 V-IoU. Table 9 adds three-split averages: Ours achieves 11.4 CIDEr versus Body-area's 10.5. These are additional experimental results, not revisions to the original scores. Agreement, attention, and concept-frequency findings are also newly reported.

T1.justification: The formal task definition, minimum-over-pseudo-label cross-entropy loss, relative-pose objective, and combined training loss are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: narration-guided learning without best-view labels, video-only inference, and superior evaluation results on two datasets. Adding LANGVIEW and 'Instructional' to the naming clarifies the already stated scope.

C2.justification: v3 interprets attention to salient moving objects as evidence of activity understanding and weak dependence on concept frequency as evidence against dominant-concept bias. It also interprets the three-split results as supporting consistency across test sets. Existing failure modes and applicability discussion are retained.

D1.justification: New Section 9 discloses eight NVIDIA V100 GPUs and pseudo-labeling costs: approximately 2.5 days with VideoLlama captioners and three hours with VideoChat2 on Ego-Exo4D, and one hour per captioner on LEMMA. Existing preprocessing, architecture, optimization, and prompt details are retained under renumbered sections.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Switch-a-view: Few-shot View Selection Learned from Edited Videos as complementary research using single-view instructional videos for training. The broader related-work discussion and positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 introduces LANGVIEW, revises the title, adds a CVPR header and acknowledgements, and clarifies narration supervision and human evaluation. The supplementary outline and section hierarchy expand, but most existing prose and the main narrative structure are preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds attention heatmaps and a concept-frequency plot, plus captioner-count and three-split tables. Existing figures and tables are retained with some renumbering, relocation, and caption edits. The supplementary text becomes more compact, while the overall two-column design remains.

improvement.justification: Compared with v2, the captioner-count and three-split experiments provide useful additional validation, while agreement and computation-cost disclosures improve transparency. The gains are limited: split construction and variability remain unspecified, and the claim of freedom from dominant-concept bias is stronger than Figure 8 alone establishes. Overall, v3 offers better-supported documentation without changing the method or original results.
